output:
To: posts/new
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Correction: the GST formula in the takings and GST template (affects v1.0 to v1.2)

Ravi Subramaniam and Shu Fen were right, and this one was my mistake.

On 3 November, Ravi's takings for the day were $1,090, GST inclusive, because his stall displays inclusive prices. The template showed GST of $98.10. The correct figure is $90. The difference is $8.10.

**What went wrong**

Column F worked out GST by multiplying your takings by 9%. That is right only when the amounts you key in exclude GST. If your takings include GST, the GST portion is 9/109 of the inclusive amount: $1,090 × 9/109 = $90.

The template applied 9% to both types of entry, so anyone keying in inclusive takings had GST overstated by 9% of the correct amount.

**Which versions are affected**

v1.0 (12 August), v1.1 (2 September) and v1.2 (1 October) all carried the wrong formula. v1.3, uploaded on 8 November, fixes it and adds a toggle in cell H2. There have been 412 downloads since 12 August. Download v1.3 from the link at the bottom of the original post, with the changelog alongside.

**Only some of you are affected**

If the amounts you enter exclude GST, column F was correct and nothing changes for you. The error only hits people keying in GST-inclusive takings, which is most hawkers.

In v1.3, set H2 to match what you actually enter: 'prices exclude GST' only for entries that exclude GST; the inclusive setting for receipts including GST collected, even if your menu prices exclude it.

**Already filed Q3?**

The error means you overpaid IRAS rather than underpaid them, so you may be owed a refund. IRAS has its own rules on whether an error like this goes into a later F5 or needs a GST F7. I am not going to state those rules here and risk getting them wrong — please check the IRAS errors and corrections page and speak to your filer.

Step by step:

1. Download v1.3 and open your Q3 file.
2. Set H2 to match the amounts you entered. If you keyed in inclusive takings, use the inclusive setting.
3. Compare the Box 6 figure on the quarterly tab with what you filed, and work out the difference — $8.10 for Ravi's one day, scaled to your quarter.
4. Check the IRAS errors page and your filer on which correction route applies.
5. Keep your original takings and your filed return as they are until you know which route applies.

One reassurance: the quarterly Box 1 sales total is calculated independently of column F and was correct in every version. Only Box 6 was affected, so your sales figure stands.

**Why I missed it**

I tested v1.0 against my own sample figures, and those figures were already ex-GST. The check passed and I took that as proof the sheet was right. I tested the one case my own data happened to cover, and called it done.

This was my error, no excuses. It did not come out of a bad file or a confusing setting — it was a formula I wrote and did not test properly. Melvin, you are right to be upset. People trusted this because I am an accountant, and that trust is mine to earn. I am sorry.

Thank you to Ravi and Shu Fen for catching it and for saying so plainly. Shu Fen, please pass this on to your group. If you get stuck, leave a comment here and I will read every one.

---

Subject: Re: your comment on the takings and GST template

Melvin, I am sorry — you are right to be upset, and I am putting up a full correction post tonight that explains what went wrong, which versions are affected and what to do next.

The short version: the template overstates GST, so you did not underpay IRAS. Please do not change anything yet. Keep your takings and your filed return as they are, and check the IRAS errors page with your filer on whether a later F5 or a GST F7 is the route for you. One thing you can take away: Box 1 was correct in every version, so only Box 6 needs checking.
